topic: How much water a household really needs for 72 hours

content.hook: How much water does your household really need?

slides.title: How much *water* do you really need?
slides.body: A simple 72-hour number for your household.

slides.title: The baseline: *3 litres* a day
slides.body: Per person, per day, for drinking and basic food prep. Three days adds up to 9 litres each.

slides.title: Do the *maths* for your home
slides.body: Four people × 9 litres = 36 litres. Write your own number down. No more guessing.

slides.title: Some people need *more*
slides.body: Infants, pets, hot weather, illness. Add a buffer for them, plus a little extra for basic washing.

slides.title: Store it *smart*
slides.body: Sealed bottles, cool and dark place. Check dates twice a year. Skip the giant container you can't lift.

slides.title: Apartment? Spread it *around*
slides.body: Smaller bottles in several spots: cupboards, under beds. Easier to carry if the lift is out.

content.caption:
Water is the first thing most people think of. It's also the thing most people guess at.

Here's a calm, simple way to get a number:

• Plan for about 3 litres per person, per day. That covers drinking and basic food prep.
• Three days = 9 litres per person.
• Family of four = 36 litres. That's about 24 bottles of 1.5 litres.

Then adjust. Babies, pets, hot weather and illness all raise the need. A little extra for basic washing helps too.

Storage tips:
• Keep it in sealed bottles, somewhere cool and dark.
• Check dates twice a year.
• Use smaller bottles, not one heavy container. Spread them around the home, especially in an apartment.

This is general guidance in line with civil-protection agencies like Sweden's MSB, Germany's BBK and Poland's RCB. You don't need a bunker. You need a number and a shelf.
